threads.body: Creating metric instruments (`create_histogram(...)`) on every call is discouraged in OpenTelemetry and can lead to duplicate-instrument warnings and unnecessary overhead. Create the histograms once (e.g., module-level singletons or cached via `functools.lru_cache`) and only call `.record(...)` during the operation.

threads.body: The A2A metric attribute group (`a2a.operation.metric.attributes` + `a2a.network.protocol.attributes`) includes JSON-RPC fields like `jsonrpc.request.id` (conditionally required when the request has an id). The scenario has `request_id` values available at call sites, but `_record_operation_metrics` does not accept or record them, so emitted metrics are missing required/expected context. Consider adding `request_id` (and optionally `jsonrpc.protocol.version`) to `_record_operation_metrics(...)` and populating them in `attrs`.

Prefer omitting the attribute entirely for non-streaming calls and only setting it to `True` when streaming is enabled.

threads.body: This streaming span currently iterates over a locally-constructed `events` list rather than consuming a real SDK streaming response. That means the span/metrics (duration, time-to-first-event, SSE event count, body size) aren’t derived from an actual A2A streaming call boundary, and `time_to_first_event` becomes an artifact of local iteration timing. Consider calling the SDK’s real streaming API against the mock server and measuring `first_event_at` from the first received streamed event.

Yep agreed @pwkowalski.   I updated the wording for this attribute to closely mirror MCP's `error.type` wording.

One open question is whether `error.type` should also be set when `a2a.task.state = failed`. My current understanding is that we should not set it automatically in that case. `a2a.task.state` represents the lifecycle outcome of the A2A task, which may include downstream agent execution. A failed task can be returned by a successful A2A request, so it seems useful to keep task outcome separate from request/protocol failure.

With that model, `error.type` is reserved for transport/RPC/protocol errors, or explicit low-cardinality errors returned in the A2A result payload, while `a2a.task.state = failed` captures task-level failure. Please clarify if this understanding is right or not.
That's a good point, I see where you're coming from here. But I think that it would unfortunately conflict with the definition of `error.type`: `Describes a class of error the operation ended with.`.

replies.body:
I researched artifacts a little further after reading these docs:

  1. https://agent2agent.info/docs/concepts/artifact/
  2. https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A/blob/main/docs/topics/key-concepts.md#artifacts

I feel artifacts are a first-class A2A concept with their own fields and lifecycle implications. Right now, modeling them as a standalone attribute tied to a task is not ideal. We need to model artifacts separately and understand which artifact properties are useful to capture as telemetry attributes.

Therefore, I am leaving them out of this PR and will create a separate issue to track how we want to model artifacts and which attributes we need to capture from them.

CC: @pwkowalski

+<!--- Hugo front matter used to generate the website version of this page:

+# Semantic conventions for Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)
+
+**Status**: [Development][DocumentStatus]
+
+<!-- toc -->
+
+- [Spans](#spans)
+  - [Client](#client)
+  - [Server](#server)
+- [Relationship to HTTP, JSON-RPC, and gRPC](#relationship-to-http-json-rpc-and-grpc)
+
+<!-- tocstop -->
+
+[Agent2Agent Protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/) (A2A)
+enables agents to communicate across vendors and frameworks.
+
+A2A conventions describe the logical A2A request, method, task lifecycle,
+A2A [`contextId`](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/#341-context-identifier-semantics)
+correlation, and streaming response behavior.
+
+## Spans
+
+### Client
+
+<!-- weaver .registry.spans[] | select(.type == "a2a.client") -->
+<!-- NOTE: THIS TEXT IS AUTOGENERATED. DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. -->
+<!-- see templates/registry/markdown/snippet.md.j2 -->
+<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->
+
+**Status:** ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)
+
+This span describes an A2A call from the client side.
+
+This span is reported by the A2A client when it initiates an A2A
+request. It covers the time to receive the response for non-streaming
+calls and the time to consume the response stream for streaming calls.
+
+**Span name** SHOULD be `{a2a.method.name}`.
+
+**Span status** SHOULD be set to `ERROR` when `error.type` attribute is
+present. The status description SHOULD match the protocol error message.
+
+A2A spans are compatible with GenAI [invoke agent spans](/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans.md#invoke-agent-client-span)
+when the A2A method invokes an agent. In that case, instrumentation
+SHOULD set `gen_ai.operation.name` to `invoke_agent`.
+
+HTTP, JSON-RPC, and gRPC conventions describe the transport or RPC
+request. A2A conventions describe the logical A2A request and task
+lifecycle.
+
+**Span kind** SHOULD be `CLIENT`.

@eternalcuriouslearner WDYM ? a2a SDK will emit two spans - invoke_agent.client and a2a.client? How does it help with anything? There is a benefit in having a predictable way to record any type of agent invocation on the client side. I.e. I can query all agent invocations in a similar manner. Or I can build a dashboard without caring how agent is called - is it an agent called with Gemini Interactions API or an agent called with A2A. If we do two independent spans, things get more noisy - they already are We can try to find means to align a2a send_message spans with invoke_agent spans. One way to approach it would be declaring a2a.send_message as *span refinement* of invoke_agent.client span with extra a2a attributes. It would be called `send_messqage` but would need to include agent name, input messages - a2a should know it, right? The concern with it is that a2a seems to be async-first and send_message is usually 'start task, something else will await for notification or poll it' - it's not invoke agent. In this case, having a2a as a separate layer is better. In this case, invoke_agent would probably be done by some higher level convenience. A2A can try detecting if it happens in the scope of invoke_agent span and then can augment existing span with its attributes.

is this more of a typical picture of a2a usage, then different layers by default and no attempts to merge them makes total sense In case of MCP we're blending execute_tool and MCP tool call because they they cover the same duration and scope.

@lmolkova Sorry, I was not proposing that the A2A SDK emit two spans, nor that every A2A operation be represented as gen_ai.invoke_agent.client.
 
a2a.client is the only span emitted by A2A instrumentation. My intent was only that, when a calling agent SDK or application already creates a higher-level gen_ai.invoke_agent.client span and invokes A2A within its active context, the resulting a2a.client span naturally becomes its child.
 
A2A instrumentation should not create or augment a gen_ai.invoke_agent.client span solely from an A2A request. For the normal asynchronous case, SendMessage, later GetTask polling, and notification handling remain separate a2a.client spans. They can share an application parent when one exists, and a2a.task.id provides task-level correlation, but we should not claim that generic A2A spans are compatible with or refinements of invoke_agent.client.
 
Your second diagram matches the model I had in mind: separate layers by default, with no attempt to merge their spans.

A concrete example is an ADK coordinator that delegates work to a remote RemoteA2AAgent.

If ADK instrumentation owns a complete delegated-agent invocation, it may create the higher-level span. The A2A Python instrumentation then creates only its protocol-operation span:
 
 ADK coordinator
  gen_ai.invoke_agent.client
   └─ a2a.client SendMessage
      ── propagated trace context ──>
      remote A2A agent
   a2a.server SendMessage
    └─ remote agent's internal GenAI spans
 
Here, ADK/application instrumentation owns gen_ai.invoke_agent.client; A2A instrumentation does not create it. It only observes the active context and creates a2a.client as its child. The common asynchronous ADK/A2A case is different. RemoteA2AAgent can send a message and receive a task in a non-terminal state, then poll later:
  
   ADK application span, if one exists
   ├─ a2a.client SendMessage
   ├─ a2a.client GetTask
  └─ a2a.client GetTask
  
  These are separate A2A operation spans, correlated by a2a.task.id; no gen_ai.invoke_agent.client is implied. A higher-level ADK integration could create one outer invocation span only when it actually owns waiting for the task’s completed result. Let me know if this makes sense or not.

+## Trace examples
+
+The examples below show the spans that can be captured when instrumentation is
+enabled at the agent, A2A, and transport layers. An A2A instrumentation reports
+only the A2A spans; an agent framework reports `gen_ai.invoke_agent.client`
+when applicable.
+
+### Agent invocation
+
+When an agent framework invokes a remote agent and its context remains active,
+the A2A span can be a child of `gen_ai.invoke_agent.client`:
+
+```text
+gen_ai.invoke_agent.client
+└─ a2a.client SendMessage
+   └─ http.client POST /message:send
+```
+
+For a gRPC binding, the innermost span is `rpc.client SendMessage` rather than
+an HTTP client span.
+
+### Asynchronous task polling
+
+When the client sends a message without waiting for task completion, it can
+poll the task. While the parent context remains active, the A2A operation spans
+are siblings; `GetTask` is not a child of `SendMessage`:
+
+```text
+gen_ai.invoke_agent.client
+├─ a2a.client SendMessage
+│  └─ http.client POST /message:send
+├─ a2a.client GetTask
+│  └─ http.client GET /tasks/{id}
+└─ a2a.client GetTask
+   └─ http.client GET /tasks/{id}
+```
+
+If polling occurs later or in a different process without the original parent
+context, the polling operations are separate traces. `a2a.task.id` provides
+the operational correlation between the operations.
+
+### Server processing
+
+On the receiving side, the transport server span can be the parent of the A2A
+server span:
+
+```text
+http.server POST /message:send
+└─ a2a.server SendMessage
+```
+
+For a gRPC binding, the transport span is `rpc.server SendMessage`.

threads.body:
I'm wondering if we could recommend instrumentations to detect if A2A happens in the scope of protocol server call and stamp a2a attributes on that span instead.

nested server span are problematic. It's common across observability vendors estimate throughput based on number of server spans. On MCP we didn't have 1:1 relationship between transport and MCP calls so we ended up with two server spans, but here we can try.

The only thing we'd lose is span name, but even that we can update after - it would be a better or similar one.

In case of gRPC it would be the same.

We can then define three versions of A2A server spans - one standalone serve, another one as refinement of HTTP server, and finally refinement of gRPC server.

we probably could even do it for clients and ask instrumentation to create transport-specific version of A2A client, but this would mean that instrumentation need to stay around protocol binding level. Looking at https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-go/blob/dda32acd9e7602c0414ef05b580730cb83d10906/a2aclient/rest.go#L47 and https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-python/issues/871 it will be wrong the moment someone configures retries.

+## Trace examples
+
+The examples below show the spans that can be captured when instrumentation is
+enabled at the agent, A2A, and transport layers. An A2A instrumentation reports
+only the A2A spans; an agent framework reports `gen_ai.invoke_agent.client`
+when applicable.
+
+### Agent invocation
+
+When an agent framework invokes a remote agent and its context remains active,
+the A2A span can be a child of `gen_ai.invoke_agent.client`:
+
+```text
+gen_ai.invoke_agent.client
+└─ a2a.client SendMessage
+   └─ http.client POST /message:send
+```
+
+For RPC bindings, the innermost span is `rpc.client SendMessage` rather than
+an HTTP client span.
+
+### Asynchronous task polling
+
+When the client sends a message without waiting for task completion, it can
+poll the task. While the parent context remains active, the A2A operation spans
+are siblings; `GetTask` is not a child of `SendMessage`:
+
+```text
+gen_ai.invoke_agent.client
+├─ a2a.client SendMessage
+│  └─ http.client POST /message:send
+├─ a2a.client GetTask
+│  └─ http.client GET /tasks/{id}
+└─ a2a.client GetTask
+   └─ http.client GET /tasks/{id}
+```
+
+If polling occurs later or in a different process without the original parent
+context, the polling operations are separate traces. `a2a.task.id` provides
+the operational correlation between the operations.
+
+### Server processing
+
+On the receiving side, the transport server span can be the parent of the A2A
+server span:

+```text
+http.server POST /message:send

+## Trace examples
+
+The examples below show the spans that can be captured when instrumentation is
+enabled at the agent, A2A, and transport layers. An A2A instrumentation reports
+only the A2A spans; an agent framework reports `gen_ai.invoke_agent.client`
+when applicable.
+
+### Agent invocation
+
+When an agent framework invokes a remote agent and its context remains active,
+the A2A span can be a child of `gen_ai.invoke_agent.client`:
+
+```text
+gen_ai.invoke_agent.client
+└─ a2a.client SendMessage
+   └─ http.client POST /message:send
+```
+
+For RPC bindings, the innermost span is `rpc.client SendMessage` rather than
+an HTTP client span.
+
+### Asynchronous task polling
+
+When the client sends a message without waiting for task completion, it can
+poll the task. While the parent context remains active, the A2A operation spans
+are siblings; `GetTask` is not a child of `SendMessage`:
+
+```text
+gen_ai.invoke_agent.client
+├─ a2a.client SendMessage
+│  └─ http.client POST /message:send
+├─ a2a.client GetTask
+│  └─ http.client GET /tasks/{id}
+└─ a2a.client GetTask
+   └─ http.client GET /tasks/{id}
+```
+
+If polling occurs later or in a different process without the original parent
+context, the polling operations are separate traces. `a2a.task.id` provides
+the operational correlation between the operations.
+
+### Server processing
+
+On the receiving side, the transport server span can be the parent of the A2A
+server span:
+
+```text
+http.server POST /message:send
+└─ a2a.server SendMessage
+```
+
+For RPC bindings, the transport span is `rpc.server SendMessage`.

+[Agent2Agent Protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/) (A2A)
+enables agents to communicate across vendors and frameworks.
+
+A2A conventions describe the logical A2A request, method, task lifecycle,

This branch and `a2a_coverage.py` can go away - the runner supports declaring the span mapping in `conformance.yaml` since [semantic-conventions-conformance#30](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-conformance/pull/30). The pin in `versions.env` is 8 commits behind and #30 is one of them; bump it and declare the mapping in the scenario instead:

```yaml
scenarios:
  reference:
    run: uv run --frozen --python 3.12 --project . python scenario.py
    spans:
      - match:
          attributes:
            a2a.method.name: {present: true}
          kind: client
          type: a2a.client
```

That also drops the silent `type_mismatch` filter in `a2a_coverage.py:_attributes()`, which today lets a wrongly-typed attribute count as covered, and it works for the server span too.
Can you add a server-side reference scenario?

threads.body:
I have one naming / layering question about a2a.task.id.

From the current wording, a2a.task.id is defined as the identifier of the A2A protocol Task object. That is useful, but I wonder whether we should intentionally leave room for this concept to connect to a broader GenAI / agentic task model.

There is also https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/issues/37, which discusses a more general task / work-item concept for agentic systems. In real systems, a task may span workflows, agents, tools, model calls, protocol operations, and even multiple traces. A2A Task seems like one concrete protocol-level representation of that broader concept.

Could we clarify whether a2a.task.id is meant to be strictly scoped to the A2A protocol, or whether it may also serve as the task identifier for the broader task concept discussed in https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/issues/37 when the A2A Task is the application-level unit of work?

If the latter is acceptable, I think it would be helpful to document that relationship explicitly. For example, an A2A instrumentation could set a2a.task.id from the protocol payload, and this value could also map to a future generic task attribute such as gen_ai.task.id / workflow.task.id when the application treats the A2A Task as the general task/work item.

This would help avoid defining a2a.task.id too narrowly now and then having to introduce a parallel identifier later for essentially the same logical task in many A2A-based systems.

+**[1] `a2a.method.name`:** This attribute records the logical A2A operation name defined by the protocol. For example, `SendMessage` is the A2A operation name, while HTTP+JSON maps it to `POST /message:send`. See the A2A specification for [core operations](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/#31-core-operations) and [method mappings](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/#53-method-mapping-reference).
+
+**[2] `http.request.method`:** HTTP request method value SHOULD be "known" to the instrumentation.
+By default, this convention defines "known" methods as the ones listed in [RFC9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-methods),
+the PATCH method defined in [RFC5789](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5789.html)
+and the QUERY method defined in [httpbis-safe-method-w-body](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-httpbis-safe-method-w-body/?include_text=1).
+
+If the HTTP request method is not known to instrumentation, it MUST set the `http.request.method` attribute to `_OTHER`.
+
+If the HTTP instrumentation could end up converting valid HTTP request methods to `_OTHER`, then it MUST provide a way to override
+the list of known HTTP methods. If this override is done via environment variable, then the environment variable MUST be named
+OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_HTTP_KNOWN_METHODS and support a comma-separated list of case-sensitive known HTTP methods.
+
+![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)
+If this override is done via declarative configuration, then the list MUST be configurable via the `known_methods` property
+(an array of case-sensitive strings with minimum items 0) under `.instrumentation/development.general.http.client` and/or
+`.instrumentation/development.general.http.server`.
+
+In either case, this list MUST be a full override of the default known methods,
+it is not a list of known methods in addition to the defaults.
+
+HTTP method names are case-sensitive and `http.request.method` attribute value MUST match a known HTTP method name exactly.
+Instrumentations for specific web frameworks that consider HTTP methods to be case insensitive, SHOULD populate a canonical equivalent.
+Tracing instrumentations that do so, MUST also set `http.request.method_original` to the original value.
+
+**[3] `url.path`:** Sensitive content provided in `url.path` SHOULD be scrubbed when instrumentations can identify it.
+
+**[4] `url.scheme`:** The scheme of the original client request, if known (e.g. from [Forwarded#proto](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Forwarded#proto), [X-Forwarded-Proto](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/X-Forwarded-Proto), or a similar header). Otherwise, the scheme of the immediate peer request.
+
+**[5] `a2a.message.id`:** See the A2A specification for the [Message](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/#414-message) object.
+
+**[6] `a2a.task.id`:** When the A2A request or response contains a single task ID.
+
+**[7] `a2a.task.id`:** Omit when the operation contains multiple distinct task IDs, for example in a `ListTasks` response.
+
+**[8] `a2a.task.state`:** When the A2A response or event contains a single task state.
+
+**[9] `a2a.task.state`:** Omit when the operation contains multiple distinct task states, including across streaming events.
+
+**[10] `error.type`:** If the request fails with an error before response status code was sent or received,
+`error.type` SHOULD be set to exception type (its fully-qualified class name, if applicable)
+or a component-specific low cardinality error identifier.
+
+If response status code was sent or received and status indicates an error according to [HTTP span status definition](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.44.0/docs/http/http-spans.md),
+`error.type` SHOULD be set to the status code number (represented as a string), an exception type (if thrown) or a component-specific error identifier.
+
+The `error.type` value SHOULD be predictable and SHOULD have low cardinality.
+Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.
+
+The cardinality of `error.type` within one instrumentation library SHOULD be low, but
+telemetry consumers that aggregate data from multiple instrumentation libraries and applications
+should be prepared for `error.type` to have high cardinality at query time, when no
+additional filters are applied.
+
+If the request has completed successfully, instrumentations SHOULD NOT set `error.type`.
+
+**[11] `gen_ai.conversation.id`:** When the A2A request or response contains a single context ID.
+
+**[12] `gen_ai.conversation.id`:** Set from the A2A `contextId` field. Omit when the operation contains multiple distinct context IDs, for example in a `ListTasks` response.
+
+**[13] `http.request.method_original`:** If and only if it's different than `http.request.method`.
+
+**[14] `http.route`:** MUST NOT be populated when this is not supported by the HTTP server framework as the route attribute should have low-cardinality and the URI path can NOT substitute it.
+SHOULD include the [application root](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.44.0/docs/http/http-spans.md#http-server-definitions) if there is one.
+
+A static path segment is a part of the route template with a fixed, low-cardinality value. This includes literal strings like `/users/` and placeholders that
+are constrained to a finite, predefined set of values, e.g. `{controller}` or `{action}`.
+
+A dynamic path segment is a placeholder for a value that can have high cardinality and is not constrained to a predefined list like static path segments.
+
+Instrumentations SHOULD use routing information provided by the corresponding web framework. They SHOULD pick the most precise source of routing information and MAY
+support custom route formatting. Instrumentations SHOULD document the format and the API used to obtain the route string.
+
+**[15] `network.protocol.name`:** If not `http` and `network.protocol.version` is set.
+
+**[16] `network.protocol.name`:** The value SHOULD be normalized to lowercase.
+
+**[17] `server.port`:** See [Setting `server.address` and `server.port` attributes](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.44.0/docs/http/http-spans.md#setting-serveraddress-and-serverport-attributes).
+
+**[18] `url.query`:** Sensitive content provided in `url.query` SHOULD be scrubbed when instrumentations can identify it.
+
+![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)
+Query string values for the following keys SHOULD be redacted by default and replaced by the value `REDACTED`:
+
+* [`X-Amz-Signature`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html)
+* [`X-Amz-Credential`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html)
+* [`X-Amz-Security-Token`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html)
+* [`sig`](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-sas-overview#sas-token)
+* [`X-Goog-Signature`](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/signed-urls)
+
+This list is subject to change over time.
+
+Matching of query parameter keys against the sensitive list SHOULD be case-sensitive.
+
+Instrumentation MAY provide a way to override this list via declarative configuration.
+If so, it SHOULD use the `sensitive_query_parameters` property
+(an array of case-sensitive strings with minimum items 0) under
+`.instrumentation/development.general.sanitization.url`.
+This list is a full override of the default sensitive query parameter keys,
+it is not a list of keys in addition to the defaults.
+
+When a query string value is redacted, the query string key SHOULD still be preserved, e.g.
+`q=OpenTelemetry&sig=REDACTED`.
+

+
+**[20] `a2a.protocol.version`:** See the A2A specification for [versioning](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/#36-versioning).
+
+**[21] `client.address`:** The IP address of the original client behind all proxies, if known (e.g. from [Forwarded#for](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Forwarded#for), [X-Forwarded-For](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/X-Forwarded-For), or a similar header). Otherwise, the immediate client peer address.

+**[23] `server.address`:** See [Setting `server.address` and `server.port` attributes](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.44.0/docs/http/http-spans.md#setting-serveraddress-and-serverport-attributes).
+
+**[24] `client.port`:** When observed from the server side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `client.port` SHOULD represent the client port behind any intermediaries,  for example proxies, if it's available.

+**[25] `http.request.header`:** Instrumentations SHOULD require an explicit configuration of which headers are to be captured.
+Including all request headers can be a security risk - explicit configuration helps avoid leaking sensitive information.
+
+The `User-Agent` header is already captured in the `user_agent.original` attribute.
+Users MAY explicitly configure instrumentations to capture them even though it is not recommended.
+
+The attribute value MUST consist of either multiple header values as an array of strings
+or a single-item array containing a possibly comma-concatenated string, depending on the way
+the HTTP library provides access to headers.
+
+Examples:
+
+- A header `Content-Type: application/json` SHOULD be recorded as the `http.request.header.content-type`
+  attribute with value `["application/json"]`.
+- A header `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4, 1.2.3.5` SHOULD be recorded as the `http.request.header.x-forwarded-for`
+  attribute with value `["1.2.3.4", "1.2.3.5"]` or `["1.2.3.4, 1.2.3.5"]` depending on the HTTP library.
+
+**[26] `http.response.header`:** Instrumentations SHOULD require an explicit configuration of which headers are to be captured.
+Including all response headers can be a security risk - explicit configuration helps avoid leaking sensitive information.
+
+Users MAY explicitly configure instrumentations to capture them even though it is not recommended.
+
+The attribute value MUST consist of either multiple header values as an array of strings
+or a single-item array containing a possibly comma-concatenated string, depending on the way
+the HTTP library provides access to headers.
+
+Examples:
+
+- A header `Content-Type: application/json` header SHOULD be recorded as the `http.request.response.content-type`
+  attribute with value `["application/json"]`.
+- A header `My-custom-header: abc, def` header SHOULD be recorded as the `http.response.header.my-custom-header`
+  attribute with value `["abc", "def"]` or `["abc, def"]` depending on the HTTP library.

+## Trace examples
+
+The examples below show the spans that can be captured when instrumentation is
+enabled at the agent, A2A, and transport layers. An A2A instrumentation reports
+only the A2A spans; an agent framework reports `gen_ai.invoke_agent.client`
+when applicable.
+
+### Agent invocation
+
+When an agent framework invokes a remote agent and its context remains active,
+the A2A span can be a child of `gen_ai.invoke_agent.client`:
+
+```text
+invoke_agent weather-agent         (GenAI agent)
+└─ SendMessage                     (A2A client)
+   └─ POST /message:send           (HTTP client)
+```
+
+For RPC bindings, the innermost span is RPC Client
+`A2AService.SendMessage` rather than an HTTP client span.
+
+### Asynchronous task polling
+
+When the client sends a message without waiting for task completion, it can
+poll the task. While the parent context remains active, the A2A operation spans
+are siblings; `GetTask` is not a child of `SendMessage`:
+
+```text
+invoke_agent weather-agent         (GenAI agent)
+├─ SendMessage                     (A2A client)
+│  └─ POST /message:send           (HTTP client)
+├─ GetTask                         (A2A client)
+│  └─ GET /tasks/{id}              (HTTP client)
+└─ GetTask                         (A2A client)
+   └─ GET /tasks/{id}              (HTTP client)
+```
+
+If polling occurs later or in a different process without the original parent
+context, the polling operations are separate traces. `a2a.task.id` provides
+the operational correlation between the operations.
+
+### Server processing

+On the receiving side, the transport server span can be the parent of the A2A
+server span:

+POST /message:send                 (HTTP server)
